open_points.subject: system_clock public operations
open_points.text: State 3 adds `system_clock` with candidate public capabilities `utc_now` and `monotonic_seconds`, while State 5 still says "One public operation per State 3 capability (100)" and defines neither operation.
open_points.question: Are `utc_now` and `monotonic_seconds` State 5 public operations, and if so what are their complete inputs, outputs, errors, effects and callers, and is the operation count 102 rather than 100?
options: Add both as public operations, with no inputs, the stated datetime/float outputs, declared backend-failure behavior, and the time-reading modules as callers; update the count to 102.
Treat them as non-public implementation details of `system_clock`, keep 100 operations, and specify how every time-reading module obtains their values without calling public operations.
Expose a clock object or port instead of two module functions and revise the callers and runtime composition accordingly.
open_points.default_guess: Add `utc_now()` and `monotonic_seconds()` as public operations and update the State 5 count to 102.

witness.initial: States 0–4 include the new `system_clock`, but State 5 contains no contract for either of its named capabilities.
events: A State 6 author writes signatures from State 5 and omits both operations because only the 100 documented operations are closed.
A module author follows State 3 and imports `system_clock.utc_now` or requires an injected clock capability.
outcomes: The generated contracts contain no callable clock surface, so the module dependency cannot be implemented from the State 5 API set.
The generated contracts add one or two clock callables with signatures and failure behavior chosen by that author.
witness.observer: The State 6 assembler and every module that needs current or elapsed time.

open_points.subject: A28 clock-reading cardinality
open_points.text: A28 first says "An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps" and expressly excepts audit `occurred_at` because "the writer takes it when it appends"; the added passage instead says the wall clock has "one reading per request" and "no second reading", while State 3 says `system_clock` performs "One wall reading per call".
open_points.question: Does "one reading per request" mean one wall-clock reading for the entire HTTP request, one reading for each application operation, or one host-clock read for each call to `system_clock.utc_now`?
options: One per application operation, with `audit_writer.append_audit` taking its separate permitted reading.
One per entire HTTP request, shared by authorization, use case and audit writer.
One per call to `utc_now`; callers independently obey their own operation-level reading rules.
open_points.default_guess: One per application operation, with the audit writer taking its separately permitted reading.

witness.initial: An active staff account exists and has no current session.
events: The staff member submits a successful login request.
`staff_identity.authenticate_staff` needs an instant for the new session and expiry.
The same operation calls `audit_writer.append_audit`, which needs `occurred_at`.
outcomes: Following the operation rule and audit exception, `staff_identity` calls `utc_now` once and `audit_writer` calls it again; the session time and audit time may differ.
Following "one reading per request" and "no second reading", the login request shares one instant, so the session time and audit time are equal.
witness.observer: A repository reader, audit consumer or verification test comparing the persisted session and audit timestamps.
